original_question: Which gene is associated with Urbach–Wiethe disease and encodes an extracellular protein containing motifs with a cysteine pattern?

final_qi.question: Which gene is associated with Urbach–Wiethe disease and encodes an extracellular protein containing motifs with a cysteine pattern?
final_qi.long_answer: Urbach–Wiethe disease (lipoid proteinosis) is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the ECM1 gene, which encodes extracellular matrix protein 1. ECM1 is a secreted glycoprotein whose structure includes repeated motifs rich in cysteine residues arranged in a characteristic pattern, matching the description given.

final_answer.long_answer: Urbach–Wiethe disease (lipoid proteinosis) is produced by loss-of-function mutations in the ECM1 gene on chromosome 1q21. ECM1 encodes extracellular matrix protein 1, a secreted glycoprotein whose sequence contains characteristic cysteine-rich repeat motifs (C-x(6)-C and other cysteine patterns). Defects in this gene disrupt the structure and function of the extracellular matrix, giving rise to the clinical features of the disease.
